long_biography.plain_text:
Hamad Ali H.A. Attiya's acquisition of Geneva Gate involved taking over an established French property company. In 2025, he and Mohammed Hamad A.H. Al-Attiya acquired the shares previously held by Partimo and Foncière Chablais et du Bas-Chablais. The business had been established in 2017, before either man's involvement.

The company's remit covers acquiring land, constructing and refurbishing buildings, and selling property before or after completion. It can sell whole buildings or individual parts, with letting as a secondary activity. Attiya became the controlling shareholder, while Mohammed took responsibility for the business as its manager.

confidence.reason: Filed articles directly set out the transfer, counterparties, share allocation and authorised object. Primary registration and the published appointment notice confirm the manager. Company remit is framed as scope, not a claim that every permitted activity occurred.

Searches returned athlete, former-minister, medical-worker and other namesakes; no name-only account is proposed. No useful owner-relevant Trip Advisor or Zillow profile was identified.

The separate readable Geneva Gate articles and public INPI extracts supply the evidence. The Pappers individual page and QNA announcement had non-retryable safe-open failures and were not retried.

The Al-Attiyah Group of Trading company brochure was discoverable but did not supply an identity bridge; the separate architectural group is led by a different patronymic name. No group business, hotel, wealth sector or website is transferred. No allegations or disputes from discovery pages are used.

The filed articles contain marriage information, but it does not establish a relevant wealth mechanism and is omitted from proposals and biographies. Shared surname and co-investment do not establish a father-son relationship with Mohammed. No private residential address is reproduced.

Birth day is directly stated as 1 January in the filed articles and is proposed at 90, below the corroborated month/year at 94. No age calculation or assumption from a generic year-only record was used.

The short and long intentionally provide a modest property-investment profile. The long describes a documented acquisition, governance arrangement and authorised business remit; it does not assert built projects, operational revenue, an education history, personal motives or unsupported public prominence.
